subject: Private deployment — operator access, customer KMS, and subprocessors
messages:
From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@brightlanehealth.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@brightlanehealth.com
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on private deploy DPA + operator access (VPC/on-prem)

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the private deployment flow looks promising. Before we move forward with procurement we need clarity on a few privacy/security points for our legal & security teams. Could you confirm the current position on: 

- Operator access: what exact actions can Redwood personnel perform in a VPC or on-prem package? In particular we need clarity around any emergency "break-glass" access, read-only telemetry, and whether SRE can ever access customer data (logs, payloads).
- Customer-controlled keys: do you require BrightLane to provide a KMS/HSM? If we provide the keys (BYOK), does Redwood store any plaintext keys, or is there an escrow process?
- Subprocessors: please send the full list of subprocessors that would have access to telemetry or maintenance channels for private deployments — including consultants and cloud partners.
- Data transfer / cross-border: any data that may be replicated or sent to US support for troubleshooting? We are EU-based customers with US entities; need to identify potential data transfer paths.

We have our external counsel (James McCarthy) looped in for the DPA side. If you have a short redline or an Annex that describes operator access scope, that would speed approvals. Can we get that by end of week?

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Kim
Security & Privacy Lead
BrightLane Health

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a targeted DPA redline and an operator access matrix that maps exact allowed actions. High-level answers below; details are in the redline.

- Operator access: Redwood's standard model is zero access to customer plaintext data in normal operations. For private deployments (VPC or on-prem) the standard is: operator actions are limited to orchestration, health checks, and non-content telemetry. Emergency support work (break-glass) is strictly time-limited, requires customer approval via an auditable workflow, and is logged to a customer-controlled S3 bucket or to your SIEM.

- Customer-controlled keys: we support BYOK. If BrightLane supplies KMS material (cloud KMS or HSM), Redwood never persists plaintext keys. We support an HSM integration (PKCS#11) and a remote-wrap flow where we only receive wrapped keys for runtime. There's an optional Escrow Addendum if customers require a neutral escrow for key recovery.

- Subprocessors: the annex lists the categories (on-prem installers, monitoring providers, selected cloud partners for Dedicated), and we will provide the specific vendor list in Appendix B. Customers can require a subset of approved subprocessors for their deployment.

- Cross-border: default for private deploys is region-local control plane. Support sessions that require logs for troubleshooting may be routed to Redwood's US support team only with explicit customer consent; otherwise logs remain in the customer's region.

I've attached two files: redwood-dpa-privdep-redline.pdf (targeted DPA edits) and operator-access-matrix.xlsx (action-by-role mapping). Happy to hop on a call with James and your procurement team tomorrow to walk through the changes.

Best,
Hannah
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference

Hannah — below is a compact proposal for an Operator Access Annex we can include in the DPA. Please vet with Legal for precise phrasing, but this is operationally accurate as to what we can commit to.

OPERATOR ACCESS ANNEX (proposed) — highlights: 
- Roles & Actions: define Operator roles (SRE, Installer, Support Engineer) and enumerate allowed actions. Allowed actions exclude access to customer content except as explicitly permitted for a time-limited emergency.
- Break-Glass: emergency access requires (1) a customer-generated RFC ticket with a time-window and business justification, (2) two-factor approval from a named BrightLane admin, and (3) a short-lived access token that is recorded in an immutable audit log. Access is session-scoped and automatically revoked after the approved window.
- Telemetry / Sampling: by default we capture non-content telemetry (CPU, memory, request latency, error codes). If debugging requires content sampling, we will only capture 1:10,000 requests (configurable) and redact PII. Samples are stored for a maximum of 30 days unless customer requests retention longer and signs a data-handling amendment.
- Key Handling: Redwood will accept wrapped keys or integrate with customer HSMs (PKCS#11). Redwood will not store plaintext keys. Any key recovery via an escrow must be requested in writing and executed under a mutually agreed escrow protocol (Annex C).
- Subprocessors: provide categories and commit to advance notification (30 days) for new subprocessors. For private deploys, customer can require Redwood to exclude certain non-essential subprocessors or require an on-site installer from Redwood partner list.
- Audit & Logs: all operator activity (commands executed, IP, agent id, start/end timestamps) will be logged and a copy pushed to a customer-controlled storage endpoint within 1 hour of session end. Logs are immutable and signed.

Operational notes/risks: 
- The 1:10,000 sampling rate is conservative; for deep memory corruption debugging we may need wider sampling but we can require customer opt-in.
- Excluding core subprocessors (for example our certificate manager partner) may increase lead time for installs; propose a 45-60 day lead time for opt-out exceptions.

I can convert this into redline text for Annex A. Let me know if the customer counsel needs more formal legalese — otherwise we can send this as an agreed operational annex.

-Karthik
Senior Engineering Manager, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah and procurement team — quick update after internal ops/legal drafting.

Summary of agreed points we can commit to in the DPA Annex A: 
- Operator Access Annex (attached as a DPA Annex) that limits operator actions by role, requires two-factor customer approval for break-glass, enforces session-scoped short-lived tokens, and mandates pushing a signed copy of session logs to your S3 endpoint within 1 hour.
- Telemetry sampling: default 1:10,000 content-sample with 30 day retention, PII redaction. Configurable by customer.
- Keys: BYOK supported via cloud KMS or HSM (PKCS#11). Redwood will not store plaintext keys; only wrapped keys or runtime tokenization. Escrow available as a separate signed Addendum.
- Subprocessors: Appendix B will include the list for this deployment; Redwood will provide 30 days notice for any change. You may opt-out of optional subprocessors but must allow core partners (certificate, installer tooling) or accept a longer installation window.

Next steps: 
1) Attached is a clean DPA Annex A redline reflecting the language above (redwood-dpa-privdep-redline.pdf).
2) If this aligns with BrightLane's expectations we can route the package to your legal + James for final sign-off and then create a DocuSign envelope.
3) If you'd like an architect-level call to walk through the break-glass workflow and telemetry hooks, Karthik and Irene are available this week.

Please confirm and let us know if you want any of the proposed limits tightened (e.g., lower sampling, no subprocessors at all).

Thanks,
Hannah
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference
